title: Statistical Analysis of the Phaistos Disc: A Computational Methodology for Phonetic Key Evaluation
description:
A rigorous computational and statistical framework for evaluating competing phonetic key hypotheses for the Phaistos Disc (~1700 BCE). The study applies Bonferroni-corrected Monte Carlo simulation across 10 candidate keys scored against three reference corpora: Luwian Hieroglyphic vocabulary, Linear A frequency tables, and the AED-TEI Egyptian corpus (675,773 tokens from 13,950 texts). Two strictly separated transcription systems are used: Evans/Godart canonical (45 signs, 241 tokens, 61 word-groups) for key-independent structural analysis, and Achterberg phonetic for G_LUWIAN phonetic scoring.

Three key-independent findings are established: (1) PLUMED HEAD→SHIELD bigram Z=+12.05 excess adjacency (obs/exp=9.7×, p<0.0001, MC n=20,000); (2) PLUMED HEAD 100% word-initial across all 19 occurrences (Z=+7.51, p<0.0001), consistent with a determinative or article function; (3) formulaic refrain structure confirmed — 7 repeated word-group sequences (refrain density 24.6%, Z=+45.60, p<0.0001). All three are robust across all parameter thresholds tested.

The Luwian Hieroglyphic key (G_LUWIAN, Achterberg transcription) achieves the highest Bonferroni-significant score among all 10 keys (p<0.0001). A blind permutation test (10,000 shuffles) refutes Zipfian selection bias at p=0.0004. Self-validation against the TLHdig v0.2 cuneiform corpus (Rieken et al. 2025; 22,116 XML files; DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.15459134) passes all five independent tests, including independent attestation of the Tiwat + water theological formula in CTH 759/761/762 ritual texts.

A blind corpus key test (200,000 trials) draws random syllable assignments from the TLHdig top-50 attested syllable pool and scores them against real Luwian vocabulary. Zero of 200,000 trials reach the G_LUWIAN score (Z=+8.53, p<0.000005), computationally substantially reducing the circularity critique. An ablation study removing all wa-tar compounds from scoring shows the signal drops by only 10% (Z=+8.53→+7.54); the result is robust to removal of the central vocabulary item.

A Ventris-style grammatical position test (4 predictions from Luwian morphosyntax) yields 1/4 confirmed (za-demonstrative Z=+3.59), 1 marginal (ha-particle Z=+1.95), and 2 failed predictions — including the na-genitive assignment, which shows the opposite of the predicted pattern (Z=−4.11). This is reported as an important null result constraining the hypothesis. An entropy profile test (T-D) confirms the disc has real bigram structure above random (MI=2.021 vs random 1.557, Z=+8.26) but direct corpus MI comparison is flagged as methodologically limited. A Ventris moment test (T-E) returns a null result: no unexpected proper names or unique lexemes recovered from TLHdig beyond the predefined vocabulary.

A working historical hypothesis proposes a Minoan scribe trained in Luwian at Milawata (Miletus, ca. 1700 BCE) as one plausible authorship model; alternative models are not excluded. The Egyptian cosmological loading test yielded p=0.178 (not significant). Token-level scores are ~94% frequency-driven; all primary claims rest on key-independent evidence. All code, data, and null results are released open-source for independent replication.

Revised Grammatical Position Test: 1/4 → 3/4 confirmed with linguistically-motivated expanded predictions (Wackernagel clitic chains, biclitic particles); §6.22 Side B Egyptian-acrophonic layer test — HIGH-confidence signs Z=+4.98 (p=0.00002) vs Egyptian theological vocabulary; §7.10 Bilateral Maritime Covenant — complete use theory: disc as bilingual trade-safety litany sealing Minoan/Luwian/Egyptian commercial agreements; three of six predictions already confirmed by independent tests; stamp-manufacturing evidence for multi-copy distribution. This work is presented as a methodology paper and a working hypothesis, not a definitive decipherment. All null results are reported transparently. Independent replication by a Luwianologist specialist is required for confirmation.
